correctness.rationale: Expanding L=D−W noncommutatively, bipartite parity eliminates unit- and three-edge terms for distinct same-class vertices. Exactly the shared-neighbor pairs contribute h²m_ij/2−h³c_ij/6, giving their one permanent crossing. Across classes, a distance-three entry is h³(W³)_ij/6; for an edge, division by hw_ij gives an upward quadratic with discriminant at most −(5d_i²+2d_i d_j+5d_j²)/12. More distant entries vanish. The stated diagonal follows since (W³)_ii=0. Every diagonal is a nonnegative spectral mixture of the cubic scalar Taylor multiplier; its derivative is strictly negative since λ>0 contributes −λ[(hλ−1)²+1]/2 and L_ii>0 ensures positive spectral weight there. It tends to minus infinity. Thus the minimum root is exact, included, and cannot be followed by a later positive interval. For F=I−hL, (I/3+F/2+F³/6) proves the lower bound and C4 has a distance-two cutoff 1/Δ. At a maximum-degree vertex, the diagonal at z=hΔ=α is the sum of (σ_i/Δ²)α²(3−2α)/6 and −(τ_i/Δ³)α³/6, strictly negative since α>3/2. For the m-leaf star at fixed z<α, the hub diagonal tends to the positive scalar cubic there, the common leaf diagonal tends to 1, and normalized distance-two thresholds tend to 3. Hence eventually the step z/m is allowed, proving liminf m h_*≥α; the strict upper bound gives the limit. Row sums equal one since L1=0. Source matrix-check code and reported finite tallies were inspected; they were not executed or used as uniform proof.
residual_risks: The all-entry classification uses bipartite parity and symmetric nonnegative conductances. This is endpoint positivity, not an internal-stage or error guarantee.

value.rationale: A local lift of a generic root test to incident degrees and shared-neighbor moments makes the largest stochastic completed step identifiable without a global matrix search, including whether a distance-two pair or a diagonal controls it. The result proves that searching beyond the first failure cannot help and gives a sharp worst-case range relative to standard forward Euler. Both effects matter for interpretation of positivity limits and are not just recalculations of known stars or regular graphs.
residual_risks: Does not claim a larger time step is beneficial for accuracy or that all internal stages or nonlinear dynamics preserve positivity.
